description: Wire the PCSX ReARMed PS1 core into the iOS build pipeline: teach scripts/build-core.sh to cross-compile it from source for aarch64-apple-ios (producing a .dylib), have native/ios/build-engine.sh stage it, native/ios/package-ipa.sh embed+sign it, native/ios/project.yml embed it, and .github/workflows/ios.yml build it and assert its presence in the .ipa. This feature CANNOT be run to completion in this sandbox (no macOS/Xcode); it is verified BY EYE by tracing every artefact path so the macOS CI stays green. A single path mismatch between what the build produces, where build-engine.sh looks, what project.yml embeds, what package-ipa.sh signs, and what the CI verify step greps for is exactly what turns CI red, so consistency of the dylib filename across all five is the core acceptance criterion. Depends on FEAT-002 (the loader must already accept the PS1 core).
steps: GROUND TRUTH (already confirmed from PCSX ReARMed master Makefile.libretro): `make -f Makefile.libretro platform=ios-arm64 IOSSDK=$(xcrun --sdk iphoneos --show-sdk-path)` sets ARCH=arm64, BUILTIN_GPU=neon, DYNAREC=0 (dynarec/lightrec is FORCE-DISABLED for iOS arm64 - so the first build is INTERPRETER-only: no JIT dependency, correct-but-slower, which de-risks the initial green build), CC='cc -arch arm64 -isysroot $(IOSSDK)', GNU_LINKER=0, links -shared with -Wl,-dead_strip, and emits TARGET=pcsx_rearmed_libretro_ios.dylib. The repo has git submodules (lightrec, libchdr) that must be initialised. Record the interpreter-vs-dynarec tradeoff decision in comments and (in FEAT-004) in SESSION_HANDOFF.md.

Add a NEW build path to scripts/build-core.sh for the PS1 core that is completely separate from the existing wasi-sdk web strategies (sources/cmake). It must NOT alter the wasi-sdk path, the RETRO_EXPORTS list, or the import-restriction check used for web cores. Suggested shape: recognise a core name like `pcsx_rearmed` (or an explicit `ios` sub-mode) that clones https://github.com/libretro/pcsx_rearmed, runs `git submodule update --init --recursive`, then invokes `make -f Makefile.libretro platform=ios-arm64 IOSSDK=<sdk> -jN`, and copies the resulting pcsx_rearmed_libretro_ios.dylib to a staging output path. Guard this path so it only runs on Darwin (uname -s = Darwin) and errors with a clear message elsewhere, mirroring native/ios/build-engine.sh. Do not fetch wasi-sdk for this path. Choose the output filename ONE way and use it everywhere downstream; recommended: stage as build/lib/pcsx_rearmed_libretro_ios.dylib to match project.yml. Add an @rpath install_name if the Makefile does not already set one suitable for dlopen from Frameworks/ (verify: if the produced dylib's install_name is not @rpath/..., run install_name_tool -id @rpath/pcsx_rearmed_libretro_ios.dylib on it, since the switch-wrapper relies on exactly this for on-device dlopen).

Update native/ios/build-engine.sh: after it builds the engine, generates the UniFFI bindings, and builds the switch-wrapper, add a step that builds the PS1 core (call the new scripts/build-core.sh path) and copies pcsx_rearmed_libretro_ios.dylib into $LIBDIR (native/ios/build/lib/) next to libcontinuum_switch.dylib. Assert the file exists after (matching the existing `[ -f ... ] || { echo error; exit 1; }` style) so a failed core build fails the engine build loudly rather than silently shipping an .ipa without the core.

Update native/ios/project.yml: add a second framework dependency mirroring libcontinuum_switch.dylib exactly - `framework: build/lib/pcsx_rearmed_libretro_ios.dylib`, `embed: true`, `link: false`, `codeSign: false` - with a comment that it is dlopened at runtime, not linked (same rationale as the wrapper). Do not change any other target settings.

Update native/ios/package-ipa.sh: the existing loop `for dylib in "$BUNDLE"/Frameworks/*.dylib` already ad-hoc signs every dylib in Frameworks/, so signing is covered if project.yml's embed placed it there. Add a fallback placement block mirroring the existing libcontinuum_switch.dylib block (if the file is not in Frameworks/, copy it from $OUT/lib/) so a skipped Xcode embed phase does not drop the core. Keep the nested-code-first signing order.

Update .github/workflows/ios.yml: (a) ensure the PS1 core gets built - build-engine.sh now does it, but the runner needs the pcsx_rearmed clone which requires network and submodules; confirm the checkout/submodule + network is available on macos-latest (it is, public internet) and add any needed setup (e.g. it clones inside build-core.sh; no extra CI step strictly required, but if build-core.sh needs `git`/`make` they are present on macos-latest). (b) UPDATE the 'Verify the .ipa' step: add an assertion that the PS1 core dylib is embedded - `unzip -l "$IPA" | grep -q "pcsx_rearmed_libretro_ios.dylib" || { echo "::error::the PS1 core is not embedded; the app would launch and fail to load PCSX ReARMed"; exit 1; }`. Keep the existing libcontinuum_switch.dylib assertion (the stub wrapper stays embedded - it is still a valid target and its harness is a live gate). Update the executable/Info.plist assertions only if a filename actually changed (it does not).

Trace the full artefact chain and write it into this feature's findings to prove consistency: [build-core.sh output filename] == [build-engine.sh copy destination in build/lib/] == [project.yml framework path] == [package-ipa.sh fallback source/dest] == [ios.yml verify grep string]. All five must reference the identical filename `pcsx_rearmed_libretro_ios.dylib`. Any divergence is a defect to fix before completing.

Because none of these scripts can execute here, run the shell scripts through `bash -n` (syntax check) for build-core.sh, build-engine.sh, and package-ipa.sh, and validate ios.yml and project.yml parse as YAML (e.g. python3 -c 'import yaml,sys; yaml.safe_load(open(sys.argv[1]))' on each). Confirm the Rust gates from FEAT-001/002 still pass (these script changes do not touch Rust, but run them to be safe).
acceptance_criteria: scripts/build-core.sh has a new, isolated iOS PS1 path that clones libretro/pcsx_rearmed, inits submodules, and runs `make -f Makefile.libretro platform=ios-arm64 IOSSDK=<sdk>` to produce pcsx_rearmed_libretro_ios.dylib, guarded to Darwin, and does NOT modify or break the existing wasi-sdk web-core strategies.

The dylib filename pcsx_rearmed_libretro_ios.dylib is used identically in build-core.sh output, build-engine.sh staging (build/lib/), project.yml framework path, package-ipa.sh, and the ios.yml verify grep - traced and documented in findings.
native/ios/build-engine.sh builds and stages the PS1 core into build/lib/ and hard-fails if it is missing.
native/ios/project.yml embeds the PS1 core dylib with embed:true link:false codeSign:false, matching the wrapper's shape.
native/ios/package-ipa.sh signs the PS1 core dylib (via the existing Frameworks/*.dylib loop) and has a fallback placement block.
.github/workflows/ios.yml verify step asserts the PS1 core dylib is present in the .ipa, and still asserts the executable, Info.plist, and libcontinuum_switch.dylib.
The interpreter-vs-dynarec (DYNAREC=0) tradeoff for the first iOS build is documented in a build-core.sh comment.
bash -n passes for the three edited shell scripts; project.yml and ios.yml parse as valid YAML.
The Rust verification gates (cargo test, both aarch64-apple-ios checks, clippy, switch-wrapper harness) still pass.
verification: bash -n scripts/build-core.sh && bash -n native/ios/build-engine.sh && bash -n native/ios/package-ipa.sh
findings:
Wired the PCSX ReARMed (PS1) core into the iOS build pipeline across five files, all sharing the single canonical filename pcsx_rearmed_libretro_ios.dylib.

CHANGES:
1. scripts/build-core.sh - Added an isolated iOS PS1 path (build_ps1_ios_core) dispatched by core name `pcsx_rearmed` BEFORE ensure_toolchain runs, so it never fetches wasi-sdk or touches web/cores/. It is Darwin-guarded (errors clearly elsewhere, mirroring build-engine.sh), resolves the SDK via `xcrun --sdk iphoneos --show-sdk-path`, clones https://github.com/libretro/pcsx_rearmed, runs `git submodule update --init --recursive` (lightrec, libchdr), then `make -f Makefile.libretro platform=ios-arm64 IOSSDK=<sdk> -j<hw.ncpu>` producing pcsx_rearmed_libretro_ios.dylib. It reasserts install_name to @rpath/pcsx_rearmed_libretro_ios.dylib via install_name_tool -id if not already so (otool -D check), then copies to native/ios/build/lib/. The DYNAREC=0 interpreter-only tradeoff is documented in a header comment. The existing wasi-sdk strategies (sources/cmake), RETRO_EXPORTS, and the wasm import-restriction check are untouched.
2. native/ios/build-engine.sh - After engine + UniFFI bindings + switch-wrapper, added step 4 that calls `scripts/build-core.sh pcsx_rearmed` and hard-fails ([ -f ] || exit 1) if $LIBDIR/pcsx_rearmed_libretro_ios.dylib is missing.
3. native/ios/project.yml - Added a second framework dependency `build/lib/pcsx_rearmed_libretro_ios.dylib` with embed:true, link:false, codeSign:false, mirroring libcontinuum_switch.dylib exactly.
4. native/ios/package-ipa.sh - Added a fallback placement block mirroring the wrapper's (copies from $OUT/lib if not already in Frameworks/); the existing Frameworks/*.dylib signing loop signs it.
5. .github/workflows/ios.yml - Added a verify assertion that pcsx_rearmed_libretro_ios.dylib is present in the .ipa; kept the executable, Info.plist, and libcontinuum_switch.dylib assertions.

ARTEFACT-PATH CHAIN (all identical: pcsx_rearmed_libretro_ios.dylib):
[build-core.sh output: native/ios/build/lib/pcsx_rearmed_libretro_ios.dylib]
== [build-engine.sh staging: $LIBDIR/pcsx_rearmed_libretro_ios.dylib (LIBDIR=native/ios/build/lib)]
== [project.yml framework: build/lib/pcsx_rearmed_libretro_ios.dylib]
== [package-ipa.sh fallback: $OUT/lib/pcsx_rearmed_libretro_ios.dylib -> Frameworks/pcsx_rearmed_libretro_ios.dylib]
== [ios.yml verify grep: pcsx_rearmed_libretro_ios.dylib]
Verified by grep across all five files (no divergence).

VERIFICATION (all pass in this Linux sandbox): bash -n on all three shell scripts OK; project.yml and ios.yml parse as YAML OK; cargo test 74/74; cargo check --profile ios --target aarch64-apple-ios --features native-core,uniffi-bindings OK; cargo clippy --features native-core,uniffi-bindings --all-targets clean; ./native/switch-wrapper/build.sh host 15/15. The macOS-only build-core.sh PS1 path, build-engine.sh, package-ipa.sh, and the .ipa build cannot run here (no macOS/Xcode) and were verified by eye + syntax/path tracing per plan.
